text:
luis: Hey team — we started seeing intermittent timeouts (30s curl timeout) from our on‑prem service to Redwood API after enabling IPv6 in our TGW. Same app works fine from EC2 in the VPC. Any guesses?

alice: Can you paste the DNS resolution + a curl attempt (with -v) and a traceroute?

luis: Sure — digging now. output:```$ dig +short api.redwood.internal
2600:1f18:abcd:123::10
2600:1f18:abcd:123::11
```curl:```$ curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/health -m 30
* About to connect() to api.redwood.internal port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 2600:1f18:abcd:123::10...
* connect to 2600:1f18:abcd:123::10 port 443 failed: Network is unreachable
* Failed to connect to api.redwood.internal port 443: Network is unreachable
(30 sec timeout)
```traceroute6:```traceroute to 2600:1f18:abcd:123::10, 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  * * *
 2  * * *
```traceroute4 to a different host (works):```traceroute to 10.0.5.12 (10.0.5.12), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1 1.2 ms
 2  192.168.0.1 5.6 ms
 3  ...
```

support-bot: auto-check: we see VPCE DNS entries for vpce-0abcde returning only AAAA records in this VPC (no A records).

sam: sounds like your on‑prem path to the VPC is IPv4-only (or preferring IPv4) and the resolver in the VPC is giving back only IPv6 addresses. If the client tries IPv6 and has no route -> immediate failure. Can you run: `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0abcde --query 'DnsEntries'` and paste response?

lu is: pasted:```{
  "DnsEntries": [
    {"DnsName": "vpce-0abcde-aws.redwood-internal.amazonaws.com", "IpAddress": "2600:1f18:abcd:123::10"},
    {"DnsName": "vpce-0abcde-aws.redwood-internal.amazonaws.com", "IpAddress": "2600:1f18:abcd:123::11"}
  ]
}
```

infra-oncall: yup — VPCE was created in subnets that only have IPv6 addresses (customer enabled IPv6 on those subnets). Interface endpoints will publish whatever ENI addresses exist. If there are only IPv6 ENIs you'll get only AAAA records.

alice: Workarounds: 1) create the VPCE in IPv4-enabled subnets so AWS publishes A records (quickest). 2) add a Route53 resolver rule in the VPC to return an IPv4 private hostname (pointing at ENI private IPv4 addresses) or put a small DNS override (bridge). 3) ensure on‑prem has IPv6 route to the VPC (TGW/IPSec must carry IPv6) so clients can reach the AAAA.

sam: Also: verify the client OS prefers IPv4 — some stacks try IPv6 first if AAAA present. If your on‑prem path is only IPv4, AAAA will cause failure.

luis: We spun up a second interface endpoint in IPv4-only subnets and updated app DNS (short TTL) to point to that — tests now show no timeouts. Thanks all :tada:

alice: Great. We'll add a note to the support KB: "VPCE DNS can be IPv6-only if endpoints live in IPv6‑only subnets — can cause on‑prem apps without IPv6 to fail." I can draft a short troubleshooting checklist if you want.

luis: Yes please — that would be helpful for future customers.

support-bot: Ticket updated: #INC-2022 - root cause: VPCE DNS published only AAAA from IPv6-only ENIs; mitigation: create IPv4-backed VPCE or provide IPv6 connectivity.
